V.rationale: Visa's fundamental health and trajectory are strong: Q2 FY2026 delivered 17.1% YoY revenue growth ($11.23B), the strongest in over a decade, with operating margins expanding to 64.4% and net income growing 31.5% YoY to $6.02B. The franchise moat is wide and deepening through VAS (27% growth, ~30% of revenue), stablecoin settlement ($7B annualized run rate), and agentic commerce expansion. However, the score is tempered by: (1) a sharp Q2 OCF decline to $3.01B (-55.6% QoQ) that cuts against the earnings narrative and cannot be fully normalized without TTM data; (2) equity erosion from $38.78B to $35.66B in one quarter, mechanically inflating ROE to 0.624; (3) missing PE/FCF yield data preventing direct valuation confirmation, though web-sourced forward P/E of 24-28x suggests a premium multiple; and (4) the CCCA regulatory overhang, though legislative progress has stalled. The stock at $321.28 is 14.4% below its 52-week high despite accelerating fundamentals, creating a potential setup. The raised FY2026 guidance (low-double-digit to low-teens revenue growth, low-teens EPS growth) and $33B buyback capacity provide a credible near-term rerating path, supporting a modest positive tilt above neutral.
key_factors: Revenue +17.1% YoY to $11.23B in Q2 FY2026, strongest growth in over a decade, beating consensus by 5.1%
Operating margin expanded to 64.4% (Q2 2026) from ~57% a year ago; net income +31.5% YoY to $6.02B
VAS grew 27% in constant currency to ~$3.3B, now ~30% of net revenue, with higher incremental margins
Operating cash flow dropped to $3.01B in Q2 (-55.6% QoQ from $6.78B), a material single-quarter deterioration
Total equity declined $3.1B QoQ to $35.66B despite $6.02B net income, reflecting aggressive capital returns ($9.2B in Q2)
ROE spiked to 0.624 vs prior 0.52-0.54 range, mechanically amplified by shrinking equity base
PE diluted, EV/EBIT, FCF yield all unavailable in supplied data; web-sourced forward P/E ~24-28x
Stock at $321.28, 14.4% below 52-week high of $375.51, down ~11% YTD despite accelerating fundamentals
Raised FY2026 guidance: low-double-digit to low-teens revenue growth, low-teens EPS growth
CCCA regulatory overhang: White House backed legislative amendment, but attempts to attach to legislation have failed
Stablecoin settlement at $7B annualized run rate, up 50% QoQ across 9 blockchains
$33B total buyback capacity after new $20B authorization; record $7.9B repurchase in Q2

sources_cited.excerpt: Net revenue of $11.2 billion, up 17% year-over-year, and non-GAAP earnings per share of $3.31, surpassing analyst expectations of $3.10
record $7.9 billion stock buyback...new $20 billion multi-year share repurchase program
Value-added services now generate about 30% of Visa's net revenue, with the segment growing 27% in constant currency to $3.3 billion
stablecoin settlement momentum with a record 50% quarter-over-quarter growth reaching a $7 billion run rate across nine supported blockchains

The White House recently backed a legislative amendment that could introduce incremental competition into the Mastercard/Visa duopoly / attempts to attach the amendment to recent legislation have failed
Regulatory risks and slowing growth threaten to cap earnings-driven rallies, with fee caps challenging high-margin models
